result.rationale: In deleteEvent (and updateEvent), the new fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the fallback branch, externalCalendarId is falsy, so find() matches nothing (and if externalCalendarId is undefined, comparison fails for every calendar), making calendarId undefined — whereas the old code fell back to destinationCalendar?.externalId. The configured destination calendar is therefore lost when no externalCalendarId is passed, breaking deletion on non-primary calendars.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the deleteEvent method in GoogleCalendarService.ts (lines 312-315), the code shows: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. This is logically flawed - when externalCalendarId is falsy (the else branch), the code tries to find a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, but externalCalendarId is undefined/null at that point, so the find will never match anything. This means when no externalCalendarId is provided, the fallback will always return undefined, and the deletion will fall back to 'primary' calendar (line 318: `calendarId || defaultCalendarId`), potentially deleting from the wrong calendar. This is a real bug introduced by the refactoring.
